To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a novel control strategy that is able to control a PM-RSM in wide speed range from zero speed up, using direct torque, flux, rotor speed, and position observers with only one voltage-current model for low speed, and only the stator voltage model for medium-high speed, with a fusion strategy for the observers, which is implemented on a dSPACE board, and validated by extensive experimental results.

a novel rotor position and speed observer for a PM-RSM is proposed, which is based on the stator flux estimation, and is able to operate in very low speeds, and that a stator flux observer for a PM- RSM in a wide speed range, using a quasioptimal flux reference, and a combined voltage-current proportional integral model, is proposed, and it is able to operate from very low to high speeds.
a novel rotor speed and flux observer with a fusion control strategy and a novel stator flux observer are proposed for a PM-assisted synchronous reluctance machine as starter alternator system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of a novel motion-sensorless direct torque and flux controlled (DTFC-SVM) starter-alternator (SA) for hybrid electric vehicles (HEV).
the development of a novel motion sensorless control strategy for a permanent-magnet-assisted synchronous machine as a starter-alternator in hybrid vehicles.
the design, development and testing of an electric starter-alternator system, based on a permanent magnet assisted synchronous machine.

the proposed control strategy for a PM-RSM starter alternator is very promising for hybrid vehicle applications.

a PM-RSM with direct torque and flux sensorless control is a viable option for hybrid electric vehicle starter alternators, with the advantages of a reluctance machine (high torque density) and a permanent magnet (high efficiency and wide speed range).
